validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, FERC-certificated interstate/intrastate gas transmission pipeline. FERC Order 149 FERC P 61,283 (Dec 30, 2014), Docket Nos. CP12-507-000/CP12-508-000 (the Corpus Christi Liquefaction + Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline certificate order) states Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline, L.P. was authorized to 'construct and operate a 23-mile-long, 48-inch-diameter pipeline in San Patricio County, Texas... beginning at a point near the City of Sinton, Texas' with 'a peak capacity of 2.25 Billion cubic feet (Bcf) per day', including the Sinton Compressor Station (MP 21.5) and Taft Compressor Station (MP 7.5). This is a Commission order, not merely the applicant's own filing. Independently, Pipeline & Gas Journal's 'Ongoing Projects' roundup (PN1018, Oct 2018) lists 'CHENIERE CORPUS CHRISTI PIPELINE LP - Corpus Christi Pipeline: Length 23 miles, Diameter 48 inches, Location Sinton, TX - Corpus Christi, TX' -- a genuinely separate trade-press origin, not derived from GEM. A third source, Oil & Gas Journal ('FERC approves Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction project, pipeline'), also states the 23-mile figure. A fourth, Cheniere's own Stage 3 Pipeline Binding Open Season notice (filed with FERC, Nov 30 2018), states the CCPL 'was placed in service on June 1, 2018' and gives its current capacity as 2,295,000 Dth/day (~2,250 MMcf/d after the standard Dth/Mcf ~1.03 conversion) -- confirming StartYear1=2018 and Capacity=2250 MMcf/d independently of the FERC order. PipelineType=transmission is correct: this is a large-diameter (48in), high-pressure, FERC section 7(c)-certificated interstate/intrastate trunk, not a gathering or process line. Owner1=Cheniere Energy 100% matches both the FERC order's corporate-parentage finding (Cheniere Pipeline is 'a wholly-owned subsidiary of Cheniere Pipeline Company, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Cheniere Energy, Inc.') and Cheniere's own current site ('an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Cheniere'). Status=operating and Fuel=Gas are trivially confirmed -- the pipeline has been continuously in service since June 2018. StartLocation=Sinton / EndLocation=Corpus Christi both hold (FERC order, PGJ, and Cheniere's site all use this Sinton-to-Corpus-Christi framing), though note the LNG terminal itself sits in Ingleside/San Patricio County on the north shore of Corpus Christi Bay, not within Corpus Christi city limits -- 'Corpus Christi' here is the metro/project-branding convention GEM uses consistently, not an error. REF HYGIENE: the sheet's existing ref for Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Start (https://www.cheniere.com/where-we-work/cc-pipeline) is a confirmed HTTP 404 -- Cheniere restructured its site. Per rule, a confirmed 404 (not a mere access block) may be replaced; Cheniere's own page moved to https://www.cheniere.com/about/where-we-work/corpus-christi-pipeline (verified live, states 'In-Service Date: 2018', 'begins near Sinton, Texas', '48" pipeline'), which I'm proposing as the replacement ref for those four cells, corroborated by the FERC order. HARVEST COVERAGE: 5 citations were harvested from this row's gem.wiki page; I opened/verified all 5 -- the PGJ 'Ongoing Projects' PDF (read in full, quoted above), the now-dead cheniere.com/where-we-work/cc-pipeline (confirmed 404), the EIA data.php link (live but a generic natural-gas-data portal with no pipeline-specific text -- a navigation surface, not citable per the egyptoil-gas.com rule), the FracTracker interactive map (live, but a JS map with no extractable per-pipeline attribute text -- not citable), and the energy.gov Stage 3 EA PDF (live; relevant to the Stage 3 loop/P2521, not P0373's own certificate, so not used here). None of the 5 needed a Wayback fallback.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM's 37.00 km = exactly 23.0 miles, which is the ORIGINAL FERC-certificated length (Docket CP12-508-000, Order Dec 30 2014: '23-mile-long, 48-inch-diameter pipeline'), independently corroborated at the time by Pipeline & Gas Journal (Oct 2018: 'Length: 23 miles') and Oil & Gas Journal. However, Cheniere's CURRENT corporate site (https://www.cheniere.com/about/where-we-work/corpus-christi-pipeline, fetched today) now describes the existing pipeline as '21.5 miles' (= 34.6 km), a ~1.5-mile reduction. Public-record trade coverage (S&P Global Market Intelligence, 'FERC lets Cheniere unit drop northern end of line to Corpus Christi...') describes a FERC order (reported as issued in Dec 2020) that vacated in part the 2014 authorization after Cheniere told FERC it no longer needed the northernmost 1.5 miles of pipeline between the Sinton Compressor Station and a Tennessee Gas Pipeline interconnect, building two short 36-inch headers instead. I could not independently re-verify the S&P article's own text (Cloudflare-blocked, and the associated Wayback capture returned an IA rate-limit page rather than content -- a network condition, not evidence either way) or pin down the exact abandonment docket/order number, so I'm not citing that article or asserting its date as fact. But Cheniere's own live site independently corroborates the RESULT (21.5 mi as the current figure) regardless of the abandonment order's exact docket. Net: GEM's 37.00 km is well-sourced as the pipeline's ORIGINAL design length, not as its current physical length. This reads as staleness (a real historical value that was overtaken by a later authorized change) rather than a fabrication, so I'm flagging rather than silently changing it. LengthKnownUnits=km is correctly formed either way.

validity.recommendation: No merge/retirement -- confirmed as a distinct physical facility from P2521. Recommend Update add a distinguishing SegmentName to both rows (e.g. 'Mainline (Stage 1/2, 2018)' for P0373 and 'Stage 3 Loop (2022)' for P2521) since both currently carry a blank SegmentName, an identical PipelineName, AND cite the identical gem.wiki page/citation set -- a latent trap for a future researcher to conflate or fold one into the other.
validity.researcher_notes: P2521 in the roster is also named 'Corpus Christi Pipeline' (Texas, len=33.8 km/dia=42in/cap=1530 MMcf/d/StartYear1=2022) and its wiki_citations.json entry is byte-identical to P0373's (same wiki URL, same 5 citations). On the surface this looks like a double-counted segment. It is not: Cheniere's own Stage 3 Pipeline Binding Open Season Notice (filed with FERC, Nov 30 2018) describes the Stage 3 Pipeline as a physically SEPARATE facility from the original CCPL -- 'The Stage 3 Pipeline will add approximately 21-miles of 42-inch-diameter pipeline loop... The Stage 3 Pipeline is proposed to originate at the existing Sinton Compressor Station, run parallel to CCPL' -- adding '1,530,000 Dth/day' of capacity 'to the current 2,295,000 Dth/day capacity of the CCPL', under its own FERC docket (CP18-513-000, targeted in-service mid-2021). Every distinguishing figure lines up with the roster row for P2521 (33.8 km ~= 21 mi loop; 42in exactly; 1530 MMcf/d exactly = 1,530,000 Dth/day) and none of them match P0373 (37 km/23mi, 48in, 2250 MMcf/d, in-service 2018). So P0373 = the original Stage 1/2 mainline (2018) and P2521 = a parallel 42-inch loop built later for the Stage 3 LNG expansion (2021/2022) -- two real, physically distinct pipes sharing one corridor and one gem.wiki article, not a duplicate entry.
